items.text: Objective, observable acceptance criteria and non-goals are concrete; the owner-selected scope and design authority are identified.

A bounded next action and priority/complexity rationale exist. The task is one complete, verifiable outcome, not cut finer than S (an outcome that is XS on its own stays one task); a child of a split records the justification for the split with the fixed cost of each pull request counted, and L or XL work records its split assessment, or a split proposal or the reason it stays whole, as the handbook's decomposition rule says.
Dependencies, release gates, serial-PR constraints and any prior agent handoff have been checked; the task is eligible to start.
Required checkout, ordinary task access, complete pinned process assets and skills are available; unavailable requirements are resolved before dependent work.
Verification evidence, review gates, risk assumptions and any operational authorization needed for the scoped outcome are understood.

For a team-managed task: complexity and required capabilities are assessed, L or XL work has its split assessment or proposal under the handbook's decomposition rule before offering, and the offer records the chosen member's suitability and cost rationale. An unmanaged task records this item as not applicable.
